_comment: English bodies for semantic-kernel (framework). Mechanism per C0-1..6. No extraSections in source; sections/sectionTitles omitted. providers not rendered — not included.

axes.model_access: Connector-style multi-model access (OpenAI / Azure OpenAI / Anthropic etc., not itemized); the positioning is embedding LLM capability into enterprise applications (official repo description: "Integrate cutting-edge LLM technology quickly and easily into your apps").
axes.runtime: **A multi-language SDK form** (C#/.NET and Python lines both release — dotnet-1.81.0 and python-1.46.0 both shipped in 2026-10, GitHub API verified): a library embedded in your application process, not a standalone runtime. GitHub microsoft/semantic-kernel 28,724 stars, last push 2026-10-30 (API verified, still releasing actively).
axes.local_files: As a library it lives inside your app, so the data surface follows your app; Azure-side services (Azure OpenAI etc.) keep data cloud-side — it splits by the connector you wire in.
axes.background: In-process calls are the main mode (library form); residency semantics follow the host application — SK itself provides no plane.
axes.tools: The skills/plugins function-calling line is the long-standing selling point (SK early on became known for the "kernel + skills" abstraction); MCP support status not itemized.
axes.context: Context management for enterprise-app embedding scenarios (planner/agent line details not itemized).
axes.permissions: The enterprise selection surface is the main axis (Azure-ecosystem auth/compliance lines follow the Microsoft cloud system); the library's own permission surface follows the host application.
axes.fit: Fits: .NET/enterprise stacks embedding AI into existing apps, the Azure ecosystem, needing dual-language (C#/Python) SDKs. Does not fit: greenfield starts — the official docs name Microsoft Agent Framework as its successor (see pitfalls).

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/framework/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/framework/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- MCP support status (not itemized)
- Coverage of the official SK → MAF migration guide (not checked item by item)
- Maintenance-status breakdown of individual planner/agent components (not itemized)
related: Same-category contrast: the same-vendor designated successor (the SK+AutoGen convergence line) — SK stays in active maintenance, MAF takes the new investment; choose by project stage.
Same-category contrast: Agno ships its own control plane (AgentOS); SK is only a library embedded in your app — "give a plane" vs. "give a library", two enterprise forms.
Cross-category contrast: both are Microsoft AI lines — Copilot is a finished assistant, SK is the base for embedding AI into your own apps — product vs. base, two faces.
